title: Thai-Style Wide Rice Noodles with Broccoli, Egg and Soy
summary: A quick vegetarian Thai-inspired stir-fry with chewy wide rice noodles, crisp-tender broccoli and soft ribbons of egg in a savoury soy-based sauce. It is ideal for a fast weeknight dinner with bright lime and fresh coriander to finish.
steps: Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the packet instructions until just tender but still chewy, then drain and rinse briefly under cold water to stop them sticking.
Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar and sriracha in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Bring a pan of salted water to the boil, add the broccoli and cook for 2 minutes until bright green and crisp-tender. Drain well.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the beaten eggs and cook, stirring gently, for 1–2 minutes until softly set, then transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the pan. Stir-fry the garlic and spring onions for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the broccoli and cook for 1 minute.
Add the drained noodles and sauce to the pan. Toss everything for 2–3 minutes until the noodles are hot, glossy and evenly coated.
Return the egg to the pan and gently break it into ribbons as you toss. Season with a pinch of black pepper and taste before adding any extra salt, as the soy sauce is salty.
Serve hot with chopped coriander and lime wedges for squeezing over.
